questions.q: What does the Flow Execution Log, as covered in course 4, actually let you see?
options: A list of every flow on the instance, ranked by how often each one runs
The execution record for a specific run of a flow, including each step's outcome and the resolved values a data pill held at that moment
The source code of the flow's underlying script, not its runtime behavior
Only whether a flow is currently active, with no detail on individual steps
questions.explain: Course 4 taught the execution record and run history as the way to see exactly what each step did on a specific run.

questions.q: A flow has been sitting at an Approval step with status "Requested" for two hours, with no error anywhere in its execution record. What is actually happening?
options: The external system the flow calls is down
The flow is correctly paused, legitimately waiting for someone to action the approval — it has not failed
The flow has definitely failed and needs a troubleshooter to fix its logic
The Connection & Credential Alias used by the flow has expired
questions.explain: No error status on the current step, sitting at Approval, is the signature of a legitimate pause rather than a failure.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say "it's been a while with no visible progress" is the wrong signal to use for declaring a flow failed?
options: Because the Flow Execution Log cannot show elapsed time
Because stakeholders are always wrong when they report a flow as stuck
Because a flow correctly paused on an unactioned approval looks the same from the outside, so failure must be confirmed by an actual error status on a specific step
Because flows never actually fail in ServiceNow production instances
questions.explain: Elapsed time alone doesn't distinguish a legitimate pause from a real failure; an actual error on the current step does.

questions.q: An IntegrationHub action step in a flow shows an authentication error in the execution log. Per this lesson, what is the likely cause and correct fix?
options: An expired or invalid Connection & Credential Alias — refresh or reassign the credential, not rewrite the flow
A missing database index, fixable by adding one
A recursive business rule trigger, fixable with an update condition
A flow correctly paused on approval, requiring no fix at all
questions.explain: IntegrationHub actions reference a Connection & Credential Alias; an expired one fails cleanly as an authentication error on that step.

questions.q: A flow's execution log shows an error at a specific REST step: a connection timeout reaching the external inventory system. What does this tell you about where the problem lives?
options: The flow definitely has a bug in its own internal logic that must be rewritten
This always means the Connection & Credential Alias has expired
The flow's own configuration may be fine — the external system it's calling appears to be temporarily unreachable
The Approval step is misconfigured
questions.explain: A connection timeout on the action step points at the external system's availability, not necessarily the flow's own logic or credentials.
